thumbnail.analysis: Actual 1280x720 and 320x180 inspected. White field; the cartoon man in sunglasses grins in a red armchair holding an open envelope stuffed with green bills while bills float around him; heavy black "THE / PAYCHECK / RULE" with a curved arrow. Mobile: three-word text dominant and legible. "Rule" singular vs title's "5 Things"; payday-windfall imagery implies spending money freely, while the script is about redirecting the paycheck; mild mismatch in tone.

script.ending_words:
who stops paying interest and
starts paying attention. So do one thing
tonight, and I mean tonight, not this
weekend. Open your payroll portal, find
your contribution percentage, find
whatever your employer matches, and make
those two numbers meet. That's the
entire assignment. It's the highest
return you will ever be offered, and it
expires quietly every year you don't
claim it. Everything after tonight is
just that same move on repeat. Your pay
goes up, that number goes up with it,
and somewhere in there the arithmetic
flips and work becomes something you
choose instead of something you owe.
script.analysis: All 17,486 stored characters read in two contiguous ranges with canonical hash match. Hook: record retirement balances alongside record withdrawals; subscribe CTA. Destination: 25x BLS average spending ($78,535 -> ~$2M); Vanguard average vs median 401k ($167,970 vs $44,115) and 4% on median. Steps: (1) match - average 4.7%/median 4%, Ella $60K 50% up to 6%, auto-enrollment 86% participation, missed-match study, true-up warning; (2) cushion - emergency-savings survey stats, record 6% hardship withdrawals, $1,900 median withdrawal cost, Josiah's raid, FDIC 0.38% vs 4%+ HYSA; (3) 22.15% card APR, $1.25T card / $18.8T household debt, $6,500 minimum-payment vs $250/month, Vanguard 3.9-5.9% equity outlook; (4) 2026 401k/IRA limits incl. 60-63 catch-up, HSA stats and invested-HSA math, Roth alternative; mid-late community CTA; (5) savings-rate years table, bank-every-raise math, auto-escalation 71%, SPIVA and Vanguard trading stats; character resolutions and "tonight" action. Highly sourced, ordered and current; one internal inconsistency. ASR not audio-verified.

claim_audit: 0:8800 BLS Consumer Expenditure 2024 average annual spending $78,535 and 25x ~$1.96M correct. Vanguard average/median 401k figures ($167,970/$44,115) are consistent with a 2026 How America Saves release continuing prior trends (not re-accessed); 4% of $44,115 = $1,765/year = ~$147/month correct. Average match 4.7%/median 4%, ~86% participation under auto-enrollment, and one-in-four missing match at $1,336/year (older Financial Engines study, flagged by the script as "last time measured") consistent. Ella's employer $1,800/year for 30 years: ~$170,000 at 7% and ~$120,000 at 5%, not $266,000 and $187,000 - and the script itself later values an identical $1,800/year at 7% for 30 years as $170,000.

0:8800 Hardship withdrawals 6% (up from 4.8%) consistent with Vanguard trend. $1,900 at 7% for 30 years = $14,463 correct; after 10% penalty and 22% tax ~$1,292 correct. Three months of $78,535 = ~$19,634 correct. FDIC national savings 0.38% vs ~4.15%: $38 vs ~$415 on $10,000 correct. Card APR ~22.15% (assessed-interest accounts), $1.25T card and $18.8T household debt consistent with Fed/NY Fed data. $6,500 at 22% with 1%-plus-interest minimums: ~257 months, ~$17,400 total - matches; $250/month: 36 months, ~$8,900-9,000 total - matches. Vanguard 10-year US equity outlook ~4-6% consistent in spirit.

8800:17486 2026 limits correct: 401k $24,500, catch-up $8,000, ages 60-63 $11,250, IRA $7,500, HSA self-only $4,400; payroll HSA saving ~$1,300 at 22% + 7.65% FICA correct. HSA asset/account counts and ~10% invested from industry reports, unverified exact. $4,400/year for 30 years at 7% = ~$415,600 correct. Savings-rate years (10% -> ~51, 15% -> 43, 20% -> 37, 30% -> 28, 50% -> 17) match the standard 5%-real/4% table; personal saving rate 2.6% unverified. Banking every 3% raise on $60K for 30 years at 7% = ~$2.34M with final-year saving ~$85,600 - correct. SPIVA (~79% large-cap underperformed; ~92% over 20 years) and Vanguard ~5% traded consistent.
